analysis: Only CHANGELOG.md was supplied (head-side text, lines 1-~197 and 198+). It is documentation with no executable change, so it cannot cause a regression by itself. It does describe code changes whose source was not in this batch, so they could not be reviewed. Items a code-level pass should check: (1) The installer served by a non-production coordinator now writes `[coordinator] url` into ~/.config/darkbloom/provider.toml (top Unreleased DevNet entry). This persists a provider's trust root across start, login, update, the LaunchAgent and the watchdog. Verify that the 'served by' determination cannot come from an attacker-influenced Host or X-Forwarded-Proto header (T-040, TB-002), and that the production installer's removal of the `url` line cannot be abused. (2) The SSD prefix-cache write budget rises from 150 to 750 GB/day (~line 198). It touches the T-041 / T-016 disk and endurance guards; the T-041 at-rest posture (HMAC names, TTL, KEK) is described as unchanged. (3) New coordinator/provider paths: devnet-seed (refuses a non-empty users table), leaderboard 503 and caching, and the Autopilot live lease and unload-victim validation. These are availability and authorization surfaces whose code was not supplied. (4) The Nemotron prompt normalization v8 and renderer v4 bump invalidates cache identities across families, with cacheSalt derived from the prompt-contract ID (T-041, SEC-035). Isolation should be preserved, but the sidecar and allowlist regeneration must be coordinated. (5) The changelog states that T-031 (the unauthenticated earnings lookup) is closed, that attestation challenges now fail closed, and that App Attest serves protocol 3 only. This is consistent with the threat model's T-036 and T-052..T-058, and no contradiction was found. The changelog records the SEC-035 TTL re-acceptance at 30 minutes, which matches T-041. No concrete security finding is supported by the changelog text alone.
